title: Bills 163 and 164 for 163-acre Central Maui growth
summary: On September 29, the Council passed Bills 163 and 164 nine to zero, after a September 3 public hearing. Bill 163 CD1 adds a 163.443-acre Kahului parcel portion to the urban growth boundary, and Bill 164 CD1 changes it from Agriculture to Business Multifamily for the Hoʻonani Village housing project. Testifiers raised concerns about water from one untested well, the airport runway, and the unfinished final EIS.

timeline.text: Bills 163 and 164 passed nine to zero.
The public hearing was adjourned.
Bill 164 CD1 would change a 163.443-acre portion of a parcel from Agriculture to Business Multifamily in the Wailuku-Kahului Community Plan.
Close public testimony on Bill 163 CD1: The Council closed public testimony on Bill 163 CD1 and accepted written testimony with no objections.
A testifier said he wants the housing built but that it could be done elsewhere with less impact.
A testifier said other land already approved for building is available near the old Dunes restaurant and the Maui Lani project.
A testifier said there would be no backup water supply if the project's single well stopped working.
He said the water supply is not certain because the project would use one well that is not yet properly tested.
A testifier said he hoped a school would be built to serve the 700 to 800 children in the new community.
He said the site is very close to the end of the runway.
A testifier said acting now is premature because the final environmental impact statement (EIS, a study of a project's effects) is not done.
Bill 163 CD1 would add a 163.443-acre portion of a parcel to the Maui Island Plan's urban growth boundary (the area planned for growth).
Close public testimony at the beginning of the public hearing: The Council closed opening public testimony and accepted written testimony with no objections.
A caller said he would support the project if it were for people under 30% of the AMI (area median income).
Another testifier said changing the zoning would be great.
A caller said the Clerk's Office did a poor job telling the public what this hearing was about.
A council member told a second testifier the bills were not about the overnight parking proposal she read about.
The first testifier asked council members to look closely at water use and land use.
The first testifier asked where the water for the development would come from.
The Council held a public hearing on Bills 163 CD1 and 164 CD1.
Committee Chair Tamara Paltin announced the public hearing on the Maui Island Plan and Wailuku-Kahului Community Plan amendments for Hoʻonani Village.

source.quote: A public hearing on bills to update the Maui Island Plan and Wailuku-Kahului Community Plan for Central Maui's Hoʻonani Village Mixed Use Development is scheduled for Thursday at 4:30 p.m. online and in the Council Chamber, Councilmember Tamara Paltin announced today.

timeline.text: A public hearing on Bill 163 is to be held on Maui before second and final reading.
The bills would change the land's community plan designation from agriculture to business and multi-family.
The council is considering bills to allow the Hoʻonani Village mixed-use project on 163.443 acres in Kahului.
A testifier asked the council to wait for a final environmental impact statement before acting on Bills 163 and 164.
The bills go to full council, where members will learn if five or six votes are needed.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The chair said the housing director will be in contact with the project representative.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Motion to replace Bill 164 with the proposed CD1 version: The committee replaced Bill 164 with a revised version (CD1) that corrects the property size.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The project team said it is waiting on water reports before moving its final EIS forward.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The project representative agreed to work with the chair on getting the word out before each chance for public testimony.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Planning confirmed a proposed zoning condition would cap rents at or below 140 percent of AMI (area median income).
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Another testifier asked the council to oppose the project or delay it until a final environmental study is approved.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: A testifier said the water would come from an old agricultural well with questionable quantity and quality.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: A testifier said housing is the biggest hurdle to keeping workers on Maui.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The project representative said a first phase of about 270 units could be ready by mid-2029.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The project representative said an existing well would be converted to supply the project's water.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The project representative said the goal is to provide housing quickly, with commercial and industrial uses secondary.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The planning director suggested waiting until a land inventory update is done and the public can take part.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The chair said a public hearing would also have to be scheduled for Bill 163.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Bill 164 would change the land's community plan use from agriculture to business multifamily.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Bill 163 would put land in Kahuluʻi inside the island's urban growth boundary.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The chair said Bill 165 would be held until the committee hears back from the Land Use Commission on the district boundary amendment.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee recommended first-reading passage of Bills 163 and 164 (Committee Report 26-34) but held back companion zoning Bill 165 pending Land Use Commission review.

source.quote: The committee held back Bill 165 proposing a change in zoning, pending a review by the state Land Use Commission.
